title: Cyrus and the Cover
premise: Sebastian Nystrom, a meticulous financial-crimes investigator, notices a single impossible anomaly: a private flight that exists in every system until it lands—then never existed at all. Chasing the vanished tail number pulls them into a laundering network run by the very regulators who trained them, and into the orbit of Cyrus Adeyemi, a disgraced pilot whose name was erased from the same records. As the network closes in, Sebastian realizes their own identity documents have been quietly rewritten too. To survive until the dawn extraction flight, Sebastian must hand over the ledger proving the conspiracy—the one secret worth killing for—to Cyrus, trading truth for escape; they land in Lagos as strangers with new names, finally visible to each other if no one else.
about_author: Orsen Oyelaran is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people the systems were built to overlook.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A routine audit of a shell company comes back spotless—too spotless—and Sebastian's unease establishes their obsessive rigor and loneliness. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the ache of a life built entirely around rules nobody thanks them for enforcing.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cross-referencing customs data, Sebastian finds flight N447CY logged in the air but absent from arrival records, insurance filings, and even the pilot roster. Emotional beat: the first crack in reality—the vertigo of holding proof that something officially never happened.

chapters.title: Cyrus
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In a coastal dive bar, ex-pilot Cyrus Adeyemi drinks to a name that no longer appears in any database, paid monthly by someone he can't refuse. Emotional beat: bitter freedom—he got everything he asked for when they erased him, and it feels like drowning.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian requests their own employment file and finds gaps where promotions should be; HR insists nothing is wrong. Emotional beat: creeping paranoia—the hunter realizing the ground under them is being edited in real time.

chapters.title: The Tail Number
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian traces N447CY to a decommissioned airfield; Cyrus, summoned to fuel a dawn charter, recognizes the investigator photographing hangars. Emotional beat: two invisible people circling the same wound, each certain the other is a trap.

chapters.title: Rules Are a Language
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts their mentor, Director Ilse Varga, who warns them off with chilling warmth: 'The rules exist so you don't have to.' Emotional beat: betrayal of a father-figure, and the seductive offer to look away and be safe.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Carried
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback: five years ago Cyrus flew one cargo run too many, discovered human cargo manifest fraud reaching regulators, and chose silence over his co-pilot's life. Emotional beat: guilt as the engine of his erasure—he didn't just lose his name, he traded it.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian copies the anomaly file to an offline drive and finds their apartment searched with surgical politeness—nothing missing, everything photographed. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; invisibility has become a weapon pointed at them.

chapters.title: Two Liars at a Diner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cyrus approaches Sebastian openly, offering the flight's true manifest in exchange for protection from Varga's cleaners. Neither trusts the other; both need each other. Emotional beat: wary negotiation, the first spark of found-family friction.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The manifest leads to a numbered account containing twenty years of regulator bribes—Varga's entire architecture. Sebastian realizes the extraction flight at dawn is how the network moves its principals out. Emotional beat: the secret worth killing for now sits in Sebastian's pocket.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus's handler activates him: deliver the investigator or be delivered. He stalls, burning his last favor, and gets shot through the shoulder escaping his own safehouse. Emotional beat: choosing a side costs blood; loyalty becomes a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wounded Cyrus and hunted Sebastian hole up in a shuttered lighthouse keeper's cottage, stitching wounds and comparing scars. Emotional beat: tenderness under pressure—the fragile first hours of trust between two people built to distrust.

chapters.title: Ilse's Version
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. Varga reviews her career: every crime she buried funded pensions, informants, order. She orders the dawn flight moved up and Sebastian's termination authorized. Emotional beat: chilling conviction—a villain who believes she is the last honest person in the room.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Varga calls personally: surrender the ledger, keep your pension, your name, your clean record restored. Sebastian hears the old hunger for belonging answer yes inside them. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate—the family offered is the one that erased them.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus steals a maintenance truck and drives Sebastian through checkpoint country toward the airfield, confessing his co-pilot's death en route. Emotional beat: confession as absolution-in-progress; Sebastian chooses not to forgive yet, but to stay.

chapters.title: Hangar 9
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the airfield they find the extraction jet prepping early; Sebastian uploads the ledger to three dead-man-switch servers while Cyrus hotwires a trainer aircraft as backup. Emotional beat: ticking-clock competence, terror transmuted into teamwork.

chapters.title: Varga Arrives
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. Varga lands to supervise the extraction, discovers the ledger breach, and faces Sebastian on the tarmac with a gun and an argument: justice is a luxury of the unaccountable. Emotional beat: ideological climax—the thesis and antithesis face to face.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian triggers the dead-man switches publicly rather than trade the ledger privately, forcing Varga's arrest by her own incoming investigators; gunfire erupts as the network tries to fly anyway. Emotional beat: the choice made—truth over safety, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus flies Sebastian out in the battered trainer as the extraction jet is seized behind them, both bleeding, laughing, airborne. Emotional beat: release—the first time either has felt weightless instead of weightless-with-fear.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Officially
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Weeks later: hearings, sealed testimony, Varga awaiting trial, Sebastian's records mysteriously intact again—but Sebastian resigns anyway. Emotional beat: grief for the institution that raised them, and clarity about what they actually value.

chapters.title: New Names, Same People
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In Lagos, Cyrus and Sebastian settle into a borrowed apartment with forged papers and honest routines; Cyrus teaches Sebastian to fly on weekends. Emotional beat: quiet joy—found family not as rescue but as daily practice.

chapters.title: The Cover
chapters.summary: Dual POV finale. A letter arrives: another flight has vanished, another name needs erasing. Cyrus and Sebastian look at each other over the envelope and, together, decide to answer it. Emotional beat: resolution as beginning—justice outside the law, chosen freely, shared.
